items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
Week6 - Data Collection

This article explains about some of the method of collecting data, pre-process them and analyzing them. It start with the data collection when the authors mentions about recording method and transcribing them. The author also mentions about the importance and also the limitation about the each of the options. Next is how to pre-process the data by coding them into several groups. These groups are either coming from the data-driven or the task specific coding. Again, the author also mention about the advantages and drawbacks of each way of coding. Lastly, the paper also discuss about the data analysis method based on the frequency analysis and sequential analysis techniques. 

I feel that this paper is good to read especially when we are preparing for our second assignment. Hence, in our second assignment, we can put small detail about what is written in the paper to convince our experiment design method.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
(Levy et al., 2012) - Monsters are people too

The experiment was conducted using primarily using quantitative measurement, as the quantitative method was more suitable for this particular research question. Investigating the question of interest involves comparing very subtle differences in behavior (eye saccade distance and position) which would be extremely difficult to obtain and measure in a qualitative way, for example by observation. Quantitative analysis of the results included comparing average vertical fixation positions across the different conditions, as well as comparing the uncorrected proportion of eye fixations on area they took up in the image. However, it seems that some qualitative information was also mentioned in the article to help determine what kinds of quantitative analyses to perform, as well as coming upon the concluding discussion:

"Thus fixations to humans and humanoids went first to the centre of the image and then immediately shifted vertically to their eyes; fixations on monsters went to the centre of the image and then moved in any number of possible directions as monster eyes were broadly distributed."

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
Bruckman - Research Ethics and HCI

I appreciate Bruckman's elaborations on the fundamental principles of research ethics, including her explanations on what each of the principles really mean and how to interpret them. For example, she explains how not to take the meaning of "do not harm" completely literally. She also teases apart the nuances and complexities involved in actual weighing of costs and benefits when considering the implications of a research study. She explains that oftentimes disparate things are being compared, which makes it difficult to directly compare the costs and benefits across them. Additionally, she mentions that costs and benefits are challenging in the context of emerging technologies because there is a lot of unexplored territory and lack of experience with the IRB.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
Diehl & Stroebe (1987) - Productivity Loss in Brainstorming Groups: Toward the Solution of a Riddle

Brainstorming is a group problem solving method to avoid members from the inhibiting effects of self-criticism  and the criticism by others. Other studies had proved brainstorming could increase the quantity of ideas. In order to find whether the three theories -- production blocking, evaluation  apprehension,  and free riding --of lower productivity have a demonstrable effect on brainstorming productivity, author conducted four experiments by manipulating those theories and type of session.

This paper provided me some concept about brainstorming still have disadvantage that real group have. Most of people in Taiwan use brainstorming in courses or activities of various fields. After reading this paper, i start to find whether there are other group problem solving method rather use the old one blindly. And i found the Brainwriting that suitable for rapid Idea Generation, someone even suggested replace ordinary paper by paper airplane to stimulate inspiration.

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
Purchase_Preface_Chap1

In this article, the author classifies HCI ideas into four classes and address corresponding HCI test which is appropriate to further research each ideas. The four ideas are A type of interaction devices associated with new hardware, A method of perception using devices that target particular senses, A method for system interaction usually embedded within other software, and finally An interactive system designed to support a complex task.

I found that my current project Knowledge Explorer is clearly a type 3 idea of HCI. According to the article I should prepare for formal comparative experiments to do further research. I think this article just provides a big picture of HCI and there are more details to understand in each idea. That's why we are provided with some more papers to read afterwards. But I think it’s a good start to have a whole picture of HCI territory.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
(Domingos, 2012) - A Few Useful Things to Know about Machine Learning

This article does a good job of reviewing pieces of knowledge that may not be obtainable from many common learning resources for the topic of ML. For example, the author emphasizes the importance of the different components (representation, evaluation, optimization) while noting for the reader that because many textbooks organize by representation, it's easy for learners to overlook the importance of the other components in the big picture. 

Tips such as warning against the ways in which classifiers can be contaminated by test data is also useful for those not yet experts in ML, as it is information that could have otherwise only be learned from becoming more experienced in ML practice. 

Including pieces of knowledge such as mentioning examples that counteract the effect of "curse of high dimensionality" is also helpful, as oftentimes in ML education students are just taught about the curse but not necessarily about cases in which it may be alright, such as using k-nearest neighbor in digit image space since this special case is a much smaller subset of possible images.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
Monsters are people too

The study set up a series of experiments using oculomotor system. A quantitative approach was employed to investigate whether there is a bias to select the middle of peoples’ faces or eyes to gaze for people. The result demonstrated that human gaze selection is mediated by a specialized brain mechanism, sensitive to the eyes rather than only the head.

In my view, the study is relatively simple but contributive, especially for individuals with autism. It can be attributed to that a specific research question proposed, "Will there be a preferential bias to select the eyes of monsters despite the fact that their eyes are not in the centre of their face?", and a quantitative approach was employed. So, the first step means proposing research questions is very important so as to influence the quality of a study.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
Week 1 : Quantifying User Research

In this chapter, the authors introduced the "User research", and give a brief knowledge about the method (emphasizing the usability test) of quantitative user study and the guideline (sample, data collection, completion rate and etc.) for it. As a beginner user researcher, I often stuck at the very early stage of a study, having problems recruiting participants and specifying the variable I want to test, and did not find significant result after the test. The importance of the randomness and representativeness is the key to a successful user study, despite the sample size, it is the way we sample and the "delicate randomness", which reduce the bias between the sample and parent population that matters.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
Week 1 : Chapter 1 (Introducing the notion of an "HCI" idea and different approaches to testing)

To come up with and propose a novel "HCI idea", it always needs some objective opinion and reflection to prove that it worth further research and will be "better" than the existing ones. The author briefly talk about how to assess an HCI idea.

Comparing to, for example, a new computational algorithm, which can be judged by benchmark, ideas including human activities cannot be evaluated that easily. Furthermore, researchers do not have that much time to wait and see the idea takes off. To refine the idea with iterative self-evaluation could define the rationale and make researcher themselves more clear about the motivation.

It is just like whenever we create a so called "new" product, we have to deliver the MVP to get feedback from the users to make adjustment for what we have missed and know more about what real users need.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
Sauro & Lewis Ch 2: Quantifying User Research

The text mentions a useful piece of information which is that "comments and most open-ended data can be turned into categories, quantified and subjected to statistical analysis" instead of using a purely qualitative way to interpret that kind of data. Having quantitative values attributed to the data analysis gives important information about the proportion of users that feel a certain way or have experienced something described by the data. This is a much more robust way to know if any piece of information was a priority, opposed to qualitative information which does not have any numerical weight attached to it.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
Sauro & Lewis Ch 3: How Precise Are Our Estimates? Confidence Intervals

It is useful to be presented with an explanation of the evolution of the Adjusted-Wald method for computing good confidence intervals suitable for small sample sizes that achieves a good balance between accuracy, feasibility and conservative nature. They explain that Wald intervals are too inaccurate, exact intervals were too conservative and expensive, and the score/Wilson interval was a good balance of those but too tedious to compute. Adjusted-Wald is meant to be a much more feasible method that uses the trick of adding 2 successes and failures to get, at a practical level, coverage as good as that obtained by the Wilson method *for most values* and even better than it for values close to 0 or 1.

Additionally, it was very helpful to know that the geometric mean is the best estimate of the center of the data for sample sizes less than ~25. For calculating central tendency, the median ignores outliers and the nature of really everything except for what is an actual central value in the data, while the mean sort of mushes together all of the data values as if they were all identical cases. What the geometric mean does which is an advantage is that it treats each data point as a scaling factor when calculating the mean, therefore taking into more account the shape and nature of the data set.

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
Amy Bruckman - Research Ethics

I am inspired about this article that has discussed clearly about the research ethics especially in HCI. I do agree that it is kind of complicated to decide what kind experiment design that will generate an interesting result but at the same time does not “harm” the participants of the study. However, this article has provided throughout explanation about what are the things to be paid attention to when designing the ethical HCI research design. In addition, I do agree with discussion about the member of IRB that might not come from HCI background. In my opinion, from the people that are not originated from HCI background, they will hardly understand the meaning or value behind every activity that are done during the experiments or the research activities design. Therefore, by not getting the common view about those reason of action, the IRB members will transform themselves to be “enemy” of HCI researcher, when the HCI researchers get their proposal rejected. It is not the matter of those HCI researchers are not good in designing the study, but it is because IRB member have lack understanding on HCI research in general. Thus, I also agree with the author statement that encourages the HCI experts to join the IRB members as well. Especially in Taiwan, where some school’s IRB members might not familiar with this HCI research field.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
Evaluation is the worst form of HCI research except all those other forms that have been tried

Zhai narrated two aspects of the importance of evaluation in HCI research in this essay. There exists some misunderstanding to the evaluation in HCI research (emphasized on user interface research), resulting a rough and not well designed experiments.

Some think that evaluation is unnecessary, and indeed, the one gets more complex, more difficult when more variables are considered, but it is true that an evaluation will always be better than researchers' intuitive opinion.

Evaluation is like the foundation of the research, just like the democracy is the foundation for modern societies. Besides, evaluation not just justified that the idea or design is better than previous research, but also give researcher themselves the insight for them to reflect, improve the design, and refine the true value of research.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
A Few Useful Things to Know about Machine Learning

This article explains some key lessons in machine learning that is hard to find in textbook, including pitfalls to avoid, important issues to focus on, and answers to common question. Since it is a very attractive alternative to manual programming, the use of machine learning has spread rapidly throughout computer science. These concepts are helpful and make me clarify some ideas. In the part “overfitting has many faces”, the article mentions bias and variance which are the same as accuracy and precision we discussed in class. I can have clearer idea how to determine the correct classier here. After reading this passage, I have more confident to overcome problems when exploring in machine learning.

items.name: 盧俊言
items.note:
Foundations of Statistics -- Frequentist and Bayesian

The paper discusses the difference between two foundations of statistics – Frequentist and Bayesian and gives the reason why we almost do frequentist but not Bayesian. Two introductions to them in the paper can obviously know that the calculations needed for Bayesian statistics can be overwhelming and different prior distribution will obtain different results. Thus it doesn’t seems objective enough.

When it comes to statistics, mathematics skill is necessary. Many people learned Bayes Theorem before. This paper deeply explains it and illustrates how to get the posterior distribution, bringing me more remarkable information of Bayesian statistics.

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
Monsters are people too

This research addresses an interesting biological question, what neural mechanisms drive gaze selection and following?
The researchers are trying to examine two proposals, one states that the gaze selection and following is arranged by a cortical neural system called STS whose main job is processing eye information; while the other purposes that this mechanism is driven by another neural system that directs fixations to the middle of peoples’ faces.
The result confirms that the gaze selection is driven by STS, and so explains that we follow the gaze by tracking the eyes rather than the middle of the faces. 

This project is quite interesting for me to read and it gives me a vary clear look at how an experiment is conducted and how to process the acquired data, by statistical means. In the studies ANOVA as well as T-test are introduced which I have yet be familiar to , so I’m going to working on understanding and utilizing these statistical methods.

items.name: 蔡守恩
items.note:
A Few Useful Things to Know about Machine Learning   

The article states that there are still some "tips" for machine learning in practical use comparing with theoretical algorithm. I have no idea about how the real experience will be since I haven’t trained any data in any project yet. Despite the fact that I’m learning the class about machine learning, the lecture still stays at the status of teaching theories and different classifier methods. I know that every topic in computer science needs empirical practice and only knowing theories is useless, so maybe I’ll try some projects after the class (maybe in winter vacation). Due to lack of the real experience, I can’t totally catch the concepts in the paper, but I believe that the tips it mentioned would be useful when I start to try some project about machine learning.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
(Purchase, 2012) Experimental human-computer interaction: a practical guide with visual examples - Chapter 1

The chapter provided novice in HCI with the notion of an “HCI idea", then described two types of HCI test: formal comparative experiments and exploratory usability evaluations.  In author's opinion, both experiment and evaluation tests are the process from designing the test, conducting it, and collecting and analyzing the data, to reporting the results. Yet, experiments are comparative and focus on producing data to demonstrate the worth of an HCI idea, evaluations focus on producing feedback to improve a system.

As far as I know, the classification the author proposed is not absolute. The book has been launched for 5 years. The notion of an "HCI idea" may not change, but the experiments in HCI are more diverse in these years, focus on not only analyzing quantitative data but also qualitative data.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
Foundations of Statistics -- Frequentist and Bayesian

The author talked about the differences between Frequentist and Bayesian Method through some example. Frequentist Method was introduced in our college statistic class earliest, is easier to implement but harder to interpret than Bayesian Method. Then, why we still use Frequentist usually? I think the point is the subjectivity of Bayesian after reading this article. Although Bayesian still has the objective interpret, the subjective one made it less weak credibility than Frequentist. But when we mention machine learning, Bayesian is the greater one. In machine learning area, we usually don't really know what is the probability of occurrence. The advantage of Bayesian analysis is that it does not require any objective estimation, just guess a prior casually, so we can do the learning to get an outcome without statistics previously.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
Martin_Chapter 2_How to do experiments

This article focus on introduce the independent variable, dependent variable, control variable, random variable and confounding variable allows you to make causal statement. In order to do experiments well, determining  those variable precisely is important step. Independent variable is the one our experimenter can set, usually contain two levels. Dependent variable is the one we want to observe and dependent on the levels of the independent variable. The prediction of the relationship between independent variable and dependent variable will determine the hypothesis is non-direction or direction. Control variable should set at a fix level. Random variables improve the external validity. Confounding variables will low the internal validity, is a bad guy we should eliminate or minimize to protect the relationship between independent variable and dependent variable from distort. Those clear explanation in this article make me set the variables about my experiments more accurate.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
MacKenzie book. Chapter 5. Designing HCI Experiments

Similar to "Martin_Chapter 2_How to do experiments", this chapter also let readers know those variable clear. So i think the more valuable part is in the second half which talked about the order effects, counterbalancing, latin squares, group effects and asymmetric skill transfer. Although most of them is mentioned by teacher in the previous class, this chapter still provide a review chance and detail explanation that made me be more vigilantly to design my experiments. And i noticed the author mentioned "It is important that the experimenter portrays himself or herself as neutral", either overly attentive or indifference or disregard will affect the participants, because in my experiments design, I may have a little interaction with participants, neutral attitude is the part I should note.
